Control’s Story And Lore Gets Weird, So Here’s What You Need To Know Before Control Resonant
description: Control Resonant is almost here, and if you're looking to jump into Remedy Entertainment's new release-- which is really good --but you're a bit lost when it comes to the story of this Control sequel, fret not; we've got you covered with a story recap in the video below. It has been quite some time since Jesse Faden first paid a visit to the Oldest House, and in the years since Control was first released, its world of paranormal threats and enigmatic entities has continued to steadily expand. Here's a breakdown of the complete story of Control so far. Not-so-Ordinary beginnings Set in 2019, the first game opens with Jesse Faden arriving at the Federal Bureau of Control, a government agency that oversees paranormal phenomena. Jesse is originally from the fictional Maine town of Ordinary, which was subject to a supernatural occurrence in 2002 that the FBC refers to as an AWE, or Altered World Event. As children, Jesse, her brother Dylan, and their friends found an old slide projector in the town’s landfill. It turns out this slide projector is something the FBC calls an Object of Power: an item from our world that has become preternaturally infused and can even imbue those who interact with it with powers of their own. In this case, the projector acted as a doorway to other dimensions when different slides were inserted into it. One of the slides housed a benevolent entity that made contact with Jesse and Dylan. Jesse described the otherworldly being as “like a star”, dubbing it Polaris, and it would be telepathically connected to her for the rest of her life. The FBC showed up at Ordinary to claim the slide projector after it caused an Altered World Event (AWE) that resulted in the disappearance of the town’s adult population and physically altered some of the kids who had discovered the Object of Power. In addition, the Faden siblings’ interaction with Polaris had turned them into parautilitarians, humans with a supernatural disposition. Parautilitarians are of…

title: Fire Emblem Fortune’s Weave Gifts Guide
description: Gift-giving in Fire Emblem games is a core staple, letting party members connect and giving tangible perks. While Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave removes the romantic aspect of support levels, it doesn't change the fact that boosting support levels is vital for recruiting new roster members and boosting stats for allies standing next to each other in combat. Where things get tricky with Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave is deciding which gift to give and when the best time is to do so. If you want to unlock as many S-Support Ranking endings as possible when you finish the campaign, then here is the lowdown on everything gift- and support-level-related. We also have plenty of other Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave tips for everything else, from optimizing how you use free time to tactical techniques for battles. The player has the option to gift a Saraminian Sweets item to a potential recruit. How to increase support levels in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Talking to an NPC with a name above their head is usually a good indication that you can recruit them if you're persistent enough. You can only give one item to any character (recruited or not) once a week, so you need to choose carefully. You can tell how well an item works in increasing your support level by the prompt you receive: "They really liked it", with two yellow arrows on-screen - double the amount of points they would gain for a big support item. (This is their favorite gift) "They really liked it" - big support gained. "They liked it" - a moderate amount of support gained. "They kind of like it" - a small amount of support gained. "They don't like it" - no support gained. In addition, you can also increase a non-party member character's support link by inviting them to eat meals as a guest. You will always have access to the menu ahead of time, and by looking at a character's likes, you may get an idea of what food is their favorite. If their name has two stars in gold, it's a good chance they'll love the dish. You…

title: Resident Evil movie review - the best video game adaptation of playing a video game
description: There's a bit somewhere in the middle of the rubbish Doom movie, where the perspective suddenly switches to first-person. Look, it seems to say, it's just like you playing the video game! But what Zach Cregger's new Resident Evil movie gets is that, really, it's nothing like me playing the video game. Back on my side of the screen, I might be sitting in a digital space marine suit, gliding around gloomy corridors as monsters leap at my face, but I'm certainly not behaving like one. I am shrieking; I am cringing, I am swearing; I am fumbling the controller, and I'm firing stray bullets at the roof. And while, yes, I might occasionally allow myself a quick celebrity whoop, the power fantasy is hardly a total one. Read more

title: Aniimo – How To Get And Use Radiant Dreamshadow
description: Aniimo is a creature-catching game with plenty of in-game currencies and resources, and acquiring Radiant Dreamshadow in the game will allow you to to change the appearance of specific Aniimo. This guide will explain how to get Radiant Dreamshadow in Aniimo as well as what it is used for. Aniimo What is Radiant Dreamshadow in Aniimo Radiant Dreamshadow is a very rare in-game currency that allows you to re-roll a legendary Aniimo's appearance to give it a new look. Radiant Dreamshadow does not alter the stats or abilities, as this is simply a cosmetic item in the game. This transmogrify option is also only unlocked once you've acquired a legendary Aniimo. How to get Radiant Dreamshadow in Aniimo Companion Handbook reward pass Aniimo is a free-to-play game with an abundance of ways to level up and earn resources without paying any money. Unfortunately, at this time it appears the only way to unlock the Radiant Dreamshadow currency is by purchasing this with real money. This item could potentially become available as a reward item for an upcoming event or other seasonal content, but right now, it only shows in the paid shop. Two Radiant Dreamshadow can be earned through the paid ($10) Advanced Edition of the purchased Companion Handbook reward track. This is found in the menus under Companion Handbook, and there is a free tier of rewards for this, but the two Radiant Dreamshadow are earned on tiers 35 and 65 of the Advanced pass. It's also not an item you can use right away, so it might not be worth purchasing if you're just starting out. How to use Radiant Dreamshadow Radiant Dreamshadow can only be used on legendary Aniimo, allowing you to re-roll parts of the legendary creature's appearance without affecting any stats. For more, check out our guides on how to find "shiny" Aniimo, unlock a free Prismana Aniimo, and earn all free in-game rewards. title: FC 27 Tactics – Best Formations and Codes
description: If you’ve juiced up your Ultimate Team in EA Sports FC 27, but are still struggling to rack up those wins in FUT Champs, then it might not be your star-studded squad that’s letting you down. The modern game is defined by systems, and ramming your CAMs into a good ol’ fashioned 4-4-2 is likely doing more harm than good. In This Article 4-4-1-1 4-2-1-3 4-2-3-1 Wide 4-4-2 How to import tactics codes in FC 27 Setting your team up for success requires finding the right formations, both in and out of possession. It can all be quite overwhelming if you’re not an armchair tactico, so our FC 27 tactics guide is here to give you the perfect starting point, complete with all the codes you’ll need to quickly plug, play, and (hopefully) steamroll your opposition. The current meta looks eerily similar to FC 26’s, though you’ll want to check back throughout the season as EA drops fresh patches that potentially shake things up. 4-4-1-1 4-4-1-1 eventually became a mainstay in last year’s game, and for good reason. You’ll be hard-pressed to find a more versatile setup, as here you have excellent defensive solidarity, the potential to quickly counter, and slowly build attacks while maintaining possession. The default approach here is to deploy two box-to-box CMs, as well as two inside forwards on either side. This naturally forms a compact unit when out of possession. Your CAM can press high with your striker, or fall back to serve as a pivot point, while your two banks of four behind them will make it difficult to get at your goal. After regaining the ball, the world’s your oyster. title: The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’s Sheik Is Nothing Without Their Androgyny
description: As a transgender woman and someone who doesn’t conform to their birth gender, there are a handful of characters throughout video games who I treat with a certain level of reverence. During my "firmly still in the closet" teen years, I found myself fascinated with Guilty Gear’s Bridget, as they blurred the lines between masculine and feminine long before their queer identity would be cemented into canon. Vivian from Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door proved equally impactful thanks to a personal arc that reinforced the woman she wanted to be and always had been. Though neither explicitly stated their queer narrative intentions, my growing mind subconsciously read between the lines, regardless: Both offered quiet forms of queer representation that, decades later, still rings true. The same compelling allure can be attributed to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ’s Sheik, a character I was first exposed to in Super Smash Bros. Melee, in which you could perform a simple button prompt to transform Zelda into Sheik and suddenly have an entirely new appearance and moveset at your disposal. I didn’t know it at the time, but seeing a cute Princess completely subvert their identity in real-time would stay with me for years to come. Prior to Melee, I had no idea the beloved male Sheikah was actually Princess Zelda in disguise--I merely thought they were another famous mascot like Kirby, Samus, and countless others I was exposed to through the platform fighter. But as I played Ocarina of Time and discovered the intended context, the brilliance of Sheik finally came into view. However, I now worry that the upcoming remake risks ruining what made Sheik such a powerful, resonant, and lasting addition to the Zelda mythos. Sheik is a mysterious character who not only guides Link on his journey, but subverts everything Princess Zelda is forced to represent. Sheik enables Zelda to present herself to Hyrule as a man who is free to navigate this fantasy world with power and…

title: I’m Tired Of Acting Like The Old Resident Evil Movies Aren’t Good
description: Did you guys hear? There's a new Resident Evil movie. Yeah! They got the guy who made the fantastic horror films Barbarian and Weapons to make it! Zach Cregger is a huge fan of the games, so there’s a solid chance it's a great movie. But you know what else was pretty good? The old Resident Evil movies. Were they faithful to the games? Not in the slightest. Were they kickass Y2K/nu-metal-drenched action films inspired by Hong Kong actioners? You bet, and I’m tired of acting like these movies aren’t enjoyable. Since Resident Evil's inception, Capcom has been trying to turn its hit survival-horror game into a hit survival-horror movie. Shortly after the game's release, several ideas were pitched, the most notable being a never-filmed adaptation from the father of zombie films himself, George A. Romero. His version saw a pretty faithful adaptation of the Mansion incident and Raccoon City outbreak that served as a metaphor for the displacement of indigenous people, and this script is actually very good and easy to find online. Yet it wasn't until Sony hired Mortal Kombat and Event Horizon director Paul W.S. Anderson, based on his work on an unmade script called Undead that was described as a rip-off of Resident Evil, that production kicked off. Released in 2002, the first Resident Evil featured an entirely new cast of characters, as Anderson believed audiences being unsure who would live or die was vital to the overall experience and would only work with an all-original crew. The film follows Alice (played by The Fifth Element star and Anderson’s spouse, Milla Jovovicha) and her fellow team of mercenaries, who are sent to investigate a massive underground lab owned by the Umbrella Corporation, yet things only escalate there. Resident Evil (2002) What ultimately ensues is a stylish and claustrophobic descent into hell, featuring creatures and gore inspired by Capcom’s games alongside an all-original story. But for as much as Anderson looked to Capcom for inspiration,…

title: KPop Demon Hunters And Ghostbusters Come To Monopoly Go For Spooky Season
description: It is officially the fall season in the northern hemisphere, and that means that Halloween is approaching. Mobile game giant Scopely has announced how it's celebrating, and that includes crossovers with KPop Demon Hunters and Ghostbusters in the uber-popular mobile game Monopoly Go. The "Monster Mash" season, as it's called, runs September 23-November 25. During the event, players can take part in themed minigames and "immersive adventures" featuring Huntr/X and the Saja Boys from KPop Demon Hunters. Naturally, music is a big part of the crossover event, with Huntr/X's "Golden" and "How It's Done" appearing in Monopoly Go during the event. There will also be new items to buy from the Blocks Boutique shop, including themed collectibles based on the movie. The characters Rumi, Mira, and Zoey will appear as well. As for the Ghostbusters crossover, there are Ghostbusters-themed vehicles coming to Monopoly Go, along with locations and characters that will be familiar to fans of the films. And before you even ask, yes, the Proton Blaster is in the update as well. KPop Demon Hunters comes to Monopoly Go. Beyond these licensed crossovers, Monopoly Go's Halloween event adds the Luck-O-Lanter, which players can fill with sweet treats they find on the game board. There is also a new "dice duel" feature where players can roll dice for the chance to trick or treat their opponent based on who rolls the higher number. What's more, the Halloween update celebrates Monopoly Go's Discord community by allowing players to vote to determine which community-made token designs actually get to appear in the game. Also, player-created tokens can now be earned in the game. Check out the spooky season trailer above to learn more.

title: StarCraft Doesn’t Sound Like An Xbox Exclusive
description: StarCraft won't be an Xbox exclusive, though Blizzard isn't exactly making it clear what platforms the newly announced shooter will launch on. Announced during BlizzCon 2026 with a 2030 release date, Blizzard's StarCraft reboot won't "be exclusive," according to Kotaku, who received a comment from a Blizzard spokesperson. What exactly that means, however, is still up for debate. When asked for clarification on whether that means StarCraft would be coming to PlayStation as well as Xbox and PC, Blizzard would only say that calling it an Xbox exclusive would be incorrect, according to Kotaku. Xbox owner Microsoft acquired Blizzard in 2023 as part of its nearly $75.4 billion purchase of Activision Blizzard. In recent months, Xbox has pivoted away from its multiplatform release strategy that saw franchises like Forza and Halo make their debut on PS5 to one once again making games, like the upcoming Gears of War: E-Day, Xbox-console exclusives. Xbox announced more layoffs today following even larger cuts from this summer as part of CEO Asha Sharma's "reset." Blizzard has yet to be hit by these more recent layoffs, but reporter Jason Schreier indicated earlier this month it could be next. Where that leaves Blizzard's various franchises is unclear. It seems safe to assume StarCraft will launch on PC, as that's where all previous StarCraft RTS games are playable. Blizzard is in many ways a PC-first developer, with a decades long history on PC across franchises like Diablo and Warcraft, and even operates its own PC launcher, Battle.net. In recent years, more and more Blizzard games have come to consoles. Diablo 4 launched on Switch 2 just last week. In a first for World of Warcraft, the upcoming WoW: Forever will have full controller support, something that is certainly making people think a console version of Blizzard's longrunning MMMORPG is in the cards. Given Blizzard announced StarCraft so early, it's possible even Blizzard isn't entirely sure what platforms the game…

title: WoW: Forever Aspires To Have A “Mandela Effect” On Players
description: World of Warcraft: Forever is reinventing the classic version of Azeroth with all kinds of new content, and if Blizzard does its job, players won't be able to tell the difference between what's old and what's new. Announced during BlizzCon 2026, Forever introduces four new zones to Azeroth: the Riverglades, Mount Hjyal, Shen'dralas, and Zephras Isle. In an interview with GameSpot, WoW: Forever senior art director Jeff Parrott and senior game designer Josh Greenfield elaborated on how Blizzard approached developing these all-new zones so that they don't feel out of place in a 22-year old game, as well as how they tried to capture how players "remember" Azeroth looking. Parrott said the team spent a lot of time looking back at the original, "vanilla" version of WoW and trying to understand how zones were designed back in 2004 when the game first released. "The team did a great job of just digging in there," Parrott said. "Riverglades is a great example. I think that's a full new zone that we have, and really did a great job of leaning into that Vanilla-era kind of ethos for the design, the flow in the way everything kind of moves through the zone, the quests move you through the zone. It does feel extremely of that era, of that time. So it's really just understanding what we're aiming for and staying faithful to it." He said the goal was for Forever's new zones to feel "familiar, but new." "It feels like going home," Parrott said. "It feels like a place you've been before. Like, 'Did this exist?' You know, if a player asks, 'Did this exist in the game?' then I think we're in a good spot." Greenfield added, "Yeah, the temporary Mandela Effect. It's like, 'I'm pretty sure this was there.' It's like, 'No, it wasn't.' 'I'm pretty sure it was.' It's great." WoW: Forever is adding major visual improvements to old Azeroth. Dramatic lighting upgrades and new water tech give zones a new look while still emphasizing their original feel. Duskwood is spookier than ever, for…

title: What Is Xbox Game Studios At This Point?
description: The organizational structure of Xbox has long been complex and unwieldy, and that hasn't changed after the latest wave of changes and layoffs as part of Xbox's "reset." But Microsoft's latest reshuffling of its studios and workforce does prompt the question of what the "Xbox Game Studios" brand even is now, with apparently only a few studios left under that banner. The Xbox division ( formerly named Microsoft Gaming ) consists of Xbox Game Studios, Bethesda parent company ZeniMax Media, and Activision Blizzard, but after some rearranging, Xbox Game Studios appears to only consist of the following companies: The Coalition (Gears of War) inXile Entertainment (Wasteland, Clockwork Revolution) Playground Games (Forza Horizon, Fable) Not included is Mojang, the Minecraft studio that Microsoft has been leaning heavily on -- that studio now reports directly to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. Graphics like this official Xbox Game Studios image from 2019 have aged poorly. Former studios under the Xbox Game Studios brand include Rare and World's Edge, the developer of Age of Empires, but both now fall under Activision Blizzard. And while it's unclear if Halo Studios as an organization is now formally an Activision Blizzard entity, it's official that Activision is indeed making the next Halo game. Meanwhile, Xbox studio Obsidian Entertainment has jumped to Bethesda, and Turn 10 has merged with Playground Games. ZeniMax now has the following studios: Bethesda Game Studios id Software Obsidian Entertainment MachineGames ZeniMax Online Studios Save for King (which also reports directly to Sharma), a few Call of Duty support studios, and whichever team is making the next Halo game, the major teams at Activision Blizzard consist of: Beenox Blizzard Entertainment High Moon Studios Infinity Ward Raven Software Sledgehammer Games Rare Treyarch World's Edge Technically, all of these development teams are still Xbox studios, and Xbox will continue to publish games from partners, like OD and…

title: Xbox Layoffs Are Not Done Yet
description: Microsoft's "reset" of the Xbox business entered its next chapter this week with the announcement of 268 more layoffs, along with other drastic organizational and operational changes for the gaming giant. As part of the announcement, Xbox boss Matt Booty said this latest wave of restructuring, combined with the changes completed in July, brings the company up to "roughly three-quarters of the way through" the planned changes. In essence, he’s saying that the Xbox “reset” effort isn't over yet, so further layoffs and other changes are expected. Microsoft's "reset" of the Xbox business is not done yet. In July, Xbox announced that it was laying off 1,600 people immediately, with a further 1,600 layoffs to come during Microsoft's fiscal year 2027, which ends June 30, 2027. With 1,600 cuts in July and 268 more today, that leaves 1,332 still to come. Even if that math isn't totally accurate given how microsoft tallies things, it's definitely true that many more staff reductions are coming. According to comments from reporter Jason Schreier this month, layoffs at the Warcraft and Diablo company Blizzard are coming imminently. This would be just after Blizzard made a series of big announcements at BlizzCon. GameSpot has contacted Microsoft seeking comment on the accounting details for the cuts so far and what could come next. The latest wave of cuts at Xbox hit Halo Studios, other first-party game developers, and the Xbox Game Studios management and central functions teams. The impact at Halo Studios appears to be significant, as Booty confirmed that the next Halo game is being made at Activision, not Halo Studios. Why is Microsoft doing this? Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who took over the job from Phil Spencer just this year, said the Xbox business was in an unhealthy place and needed to be overhauled. She cited a number of reasons, including Microsoft's big bet on Game Pass simply not working out and the shift away from exclusives promoted by Spencer and Sarah Bond eating away…

title: WoW: Forever Doesn’t Let Shamans Or Warlocks Tank, But That Could Change
description: World of Warcraft: Forever is bringing big changes to the WoW Classic sandbox, but don't expect to see Shamans or Warlocks tanking, at least at launch. New roles for classes, like the above-mentioned tanks, as well as Rogue tank and Mage healer, were something Blizzard experimented with in WoW: Classic Season of Discovery. It certainly helped solve the game's tank shortage problem, with more classes than ever before able to taunt enemies and effectively hold aggro. In an interview with GameSpot, WoW: Forever senior game designer Josh Greenfield said that while the team learned many lessons with Season of Discovery and carried many of those forward into Forever, more "out there" changes like Warlock tank or Mage healer didn't make the jump. “I think in spirit, a lot of the lessons we learned are carried over, but some of the more out-there things that weren’t originally in original WoW, we tone them back a little bit,” Greenfield said. “Because it’s one of those things…It’s in the name: It’s Forever. We can do a lot of things over years, but we wanted to kind of start from a place where the soul of the class is very coded and original-WoW-centric. But there’s still meaningful changes and really exciting kinds of ways to play, the existing ways to play your class and new ways to play your class. But some of [those], like Warlock tank, Shaman tank, not quite yet, but never say never." Currently in the WoW: Forever beta, the idea of a tank Shaman is much as it was in original WoW: something that is on the cusp of being viable, but is still held back by things like the lack of a true taunt and better damage mitigation. It wouldn't take too many changes for Shaman to become become a proper tank once again, though when or if that will actually happen is up in the air. Some Season of Discovery content that has made its way into Forever. It's been confirmed that certain pieces of the experimental season, like new class quests, the Undermine Reals endgame currency, and even…

title: Prebuilt Steam Machine faceplate screens are here, delivering decent, surprisingly cheaper alternatives to Valve-approved DIY builds
description: If you own a Steam Machine, and still cling to the misconception that my budget faceplate ideas aren’t good enough for you, you basically have three options for front panel customisation. The first is to grab something off Etsy or suchlike. The second is take advantage of Valve’s open-source Inkterface project to build yourself an E-Ink display, onto which you can electronically daub performance monitoring info. The third is to end up with more or less the same panel as option two, but have someone else make it for you. That’s what arch accessory makers JSAUX are proposing with their Steam Machine E-Ink and Pixel Matrix faceplates, which go on sale today after a few weeks of preening around the case mod scene. I’ve been using both on my Machine at home, and they’re quite good fun. The E-Ink faceplate, for which I sense the greater internet buzz, is a crisp, tidy little black-and-white panel, while the PixelMatrix trades detail density for colour and retro charm. Both have a few different display modes, switchable in SteamOS’s quick settings menu (via some clever integration with the Decky Loader plugin tool), and while I had to set this up manually, JSAUX say the requisite software will be downloadable via Steam itself from early October. Truly, it’s all the results of a DIY mod and more, conveniently pre-prepared for people who don’t own soldering irons. Read more

title: "I'm still blown away by the amount of talent": Hellblade devs Ninja Theory face closure after Microsoft fail to reach a deal with buyers
description: Earlier this year, Microsoft announced that they were trying to sell UK-based Hellblade creators Ninja Theory as part of their steady efforts to siphon larger, shinier doubloons from the Xbox gaming business by laying off thousands of people. Today, they are proposing to close Ninja Theory, having ultimately failed to reach an agreement with buyers, though they're still holding out hope of a happier outcome. The news comes as part of the latest round of Microsoft cuts, which have seen Xbox lay off 268 people and merge several of their best-known studios. Read more
